statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: miR-223-based therapy produced durable tumour responses in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
statements.evidence: The current treatment for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) to block angiogenesis and immunosuppression provides some benefits only for a subset of patients with HCC
statements.note: The abstract discusses existing patient therapies and mouse experiments but reports no miR-223 treatment given to patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Compared with wild-type animals, miR-223 knockout mice accumulated more PD-1+ T cells and PD-L1+ macrophages after DEN plus CCl4 treatment.
statements.evidence: Compared with wild-type mice, miR-223 knockout mice had more infiltrated programmed cell death 1 (PD-1 + ) T cells and programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1 + ) macrophages after DEN+CCl 4 administration.
statements.note: The study reports knockout mice had more infiltrated PD-1+ T cells and PD-L1+ macrophages than wild-type mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: miR-223 did not bind PD-1 or PD-L1 directly but lowered them indirectly by blocking the hypoxia-inducible-factor-driven CD39/CD73-adenosine pathway.
statements.evidence: miR-223 did not directly target PD-1 and PD-L1 in immune cells rather than indirectly downregulated them by modulating tumour microenvironment via the suppression of hypoxia-inducible factor
statements.note: The abstract states miR-223 downregulated PD-1/PD-L1 indirectly, by suppressing the hypoxia-inducible-factor-driven CD39/CD73-adenosine pathway, not by direct targeting.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adenoviral delivery of miR-223 blocked angiogenesis and hypoxia-driven PD-1/PD-L1 activation in both HCC models, slowing tumour progression.
statements.evidence: gene delivery of miR-223 via adenovirus inhibited angiogenesis and hypoxia-mediated PD-1/PD-L1 activation in both HCC models
statements.note: Adenovirus-delivered miR-223 inhibited angiogenesis and hypoxia-mediated PD-1/PD-L1 activation in both models, hindering progression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A 14-amino-acid peptide at the C-terminus of TaHSFA6e-III, produced by alternative splicing, is predicted to fold into an amphipathic helix.
statements.evidence: the enhanced transcriptional activity of TaHSFA6e-III is due to a 14-amino acid peptide at its C-terminus, which arises from alternative splicing and is predicted to form an amphipathic helix.
statements.note: The abstract attributes TaHSFA6e-III's stronger activity to a 14-amino-acid C-terminal peptide predicted to form an amphipathic helix.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking out either TaHSFA6e or TaHSP70s renders wheat plants sensitive to heat.
statements.evidence: knockout of TaHSFA6e or TaHSP70s increases heat sensitivity in wheat.
statements.note: The study shows that eliminating TaHSFA6e or TaHSP70s raises heat sensitivity in wheat.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Overexpressing TaHSFA6e-III increased grain yield in field-grown wheat under heat.
statements.evidence: Heat stress greatly threatens crop production.
statements.note: The abstract motivates the work with crop production but reports no grain-yield or field measurements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: TaHSFA6e-III boosts transcription of three downstream TaHSP70 genes to a greater extent than TaHSFA6e-II does.
statements.evidence: TaHSFA6e-III enhances the transcriptional activity of three downstream heat shock protein 70 (TaHSP70) genes to a greater extent than does TaHSFA6e-II.
statements.note: The study found TaHSFA6e-III activated the three TaHSP70 genes more strongly than TaHSFA6e-II.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Validated circRNAs were generated by 29% of Parkinson's-associated genes and 12% of Alzheimer's-associated genes.
statements.evidence: 29% of Parkinson's and 12% of Alzheimer's disease-associated genes produced validated circRNAs.
statements.note: The study reports validated circRNAs from 29% of Parkinson's and 12% of Alzheimer's disease-associated genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Circulating circDNAJC6 levels serve as a blood biomarker for early Parkinson's disease.
statements.evidence: circDNAJC6, which is transcribed from a juvenile-onset Parkinson's gene, is already dysregulated during prodromal, onset stages of common Parkinson's disease neuropathology.
statements.note: Early dysregulation of circDNAJC6 is reported, but its use as a measurable blood biomarker was not tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The 1526 and 3308 cell-type-specific circRNAs of dopamine and pyramidal neurons were enriched in synapse pathways.
statements.evidence: 1526 and 3308 circRNAs are custom-tailored to the cell identity of dopamine and pyramidal neurons and enriched in synapse pathways.
statements.note: The study found the neuron-specific circRNAs were enriched in synapse pathways.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ultra-deep total RNA sequencing catalogued over 11,039 circRNAs across dopamine neurons, pyramidal neurons, and non-neuronal cells from 190 human brains.
statements.evidence: we systematically identify over 11,039 circRNAs expressed in vulnerable dopamine and pyramidal neurons laser-captured from 190 human brains and non-neuronal cells using ultra-deep, total RNA sequencing
statements.note: The authors identified more than 11,039 circRNAs across these cell types from 190 human brains.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PTBP1 and PTBP2 bind SYNGAP1 transcripts directly and drive inclusion of its alternative 3' splice site.
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that PTBP1/2 directly bind to and promote SYNGAP1 A3SS inclusion.
statements.note: The study demonstrates that PTBP1/2 directly bind SYNGAP1 and promote inclusion of its A3SS.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A splice-switching oligonucleotide converted the unproductive SYNGAP1 isoform into the functional form in human iPSC-derived neurons.
statements.evidence: We further report a splice-switching oligonucleotide (SSO) that converts SYNGAP1 unproductive isoform to the functional form in human iPSC-derived neurons.
statements.note: The authors report an SSO that switches the unproductive SYNGAP1 isoform to the functional form in human iPSC neurons.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting the Syngap1 A3SS in mice increased Syngap1 protein and rescued the long-term potentiation and membrane excitability deficits of a knockout allele.
statements.evidence: Genetic deletion of the Syngap1 A3SS in mice upregulates Syngap1 protein and alleviates the long-term potentiation and membrane excitability deficits caused by a Syngap1 knockout allele.
statements.note: Removing the A3SS raised Syngap1 protein and relieved the LTP and excitability deficits caused by a knockout allele.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The splice-switching oligonucleotide reversed autism-like behaviours in Syngap1 mutant mice.
statements.evidence: the development of an SSO to potentially alleviate SYNGAP1-associated haploinsufficiency.
statements.note: The abstract reports molecular and physiological rescue but no behavioural outcomes in mice treated with the SSO.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LITATS1 drives polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of the TGF-β type I receptor (TβRI).
statements.evidence: Mechanistically, LITATS1 enhances the polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of TGF-β type I receptor (TβRI).
statements.note: Mechanistically, LITATS1 promotes polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of the TGF-β type I receptor.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LITATS1 levels are reduced in lung adenocarcinoma relative to adjacent normal tissue and track with better prognosis in breast and lung cancer patients.
statements.evidence: LITATS1 expression is reduced in lung adenocarcinoma tissues compared with adjacent normal tissues and correlates with a favorable prognosis in breast and non-small cell lung cancer patients.
statements.note: LITATS1 is expressed at lower levels in lung adenocarcinoma than adjacent normal tissue and associates with favourable prognosis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Restoring LITATS1 expression suppressed tumour growth in breast cancer xenograft models.
statements.evidence: LITATS1 depletion promotes TGF-β-induced EMT, migration, and extravasation in cancer cells.
statements.note: Depletion effects on EMT, migration and extravasation are shown, but LITATS1 restoration in animal tumour models was not tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LITATS1 acts as an epithelial gatekeeper and blocks EMT in breast and non-small cell lung cancer cells.
statements.evidence: the long noncoding RNA LITATS1 (LINC01137, ZC3H12A-DT) is an epithelial gatekeeper in normal epithelial cells and inhibits EMT in breast and non-small cell lung cancer cells.
statements.note: The study reports LITATS1 is an epithelial gatekeeper that inhibits EMT in breast and NSCLC cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Aging trajectories were mostly tissue-specific apart from eight microRNAs that were broadly deregulated throughout the body.
statements.evidence: We found molecular aging trajectories are largely tissue-specific except for eight broadly deregulated microRNAs (miRNAs).
statements.note: The study found aging trajectories largely tissue-specific, except for eight broadly deregulated miRNAs.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Lowering miR-29c-3p extended lifespan in aged mice.
statements.evidence: miR-29c-3p targets the extracellular matrix and secretion pathways, known to be implicated in aging.
statements.note: miR-29c-3p's targets are described, but no experiment manipulated it to change lifespan.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The authors built a body-wide ncRNA expression map covering 16 organs at ten timepoints from 1 to 27 months in aging and rejuvenated mice.
statements.evidence: a body-wide map of noncoding RNA (ncRNA) expression in aging (16 organs at ten timepoints from 1 to 27 months) and rejuvenated mice
statements.note: They generated an organism-wide ncRNA map across 16 organs and ten timepoints in aging and rejuvenated mice.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In mice rejuvenated by heterochronic parabiosis, miR-29c-3p was the most prominent miRNA restored toward the levels seen in young liver.
statements.evidence: In mice rejuvenated by heterochronic parabiosis, miR-29c-3p was the most prominent miRNA restored to similar levels found in young liver.
statements.note: In parabiosis-rejuvenated mice, miR-29c-3p was the most prominently restored miRNA, returning toward young-liver levels.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Antisense-oligonucleotide inhibition of Malat1 blocked metastasis, and the effect depended on SERPINB6B.
statements.evidence: On-target inhibition of Malat1 using therapeutic antisense nucleotides suppresses metastasis in a SERPINB6B-dependent manner.
statements.note: Therapeutic antisense inhibition of Malat1 suppressed metastasis in a SERPINB6B-dependent way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The lncRNA Malat1 is necessary for tumour initiation and metastatic reactivation in mouse models of breast cancer and other tumour types.
statements.evidence: the long noncoding RNA Malat1 is required for tumor initiation and metastatic reactivation in mouse models of breast cancer and other tumor types.
statements.note: The study shows Malat1 is required for tumour initiation and metastatic reactivation across several mouse tumour models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In metastatic cells, SERPINB6B suppresses immunogenic cell death and lets tumour cells evade T-cell-mediated lysis.
statements.evidence: SERPINB6B suppresses immunogenic cell death and confers evasion of T cell-mediated tumor lysis of incipient metastatic cells.
statements.note: SERPINB6B blocks immunogenic cell death, letting incipient metastatic cells escape T-cell-mediated lysis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Malat1 expression levels predict relapse risk in breast cancer patients.
statements.evidence: Thus, Malat1 is at the nexus of tumor initiation, reactivation and immune evasion and represents a tractable and clinically relevant drug target.
statements.note: Malat1 is called a clinically relevant drug target, but no patient relapse or prognostic data are reported.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: LIPTER is lower in heart tissue of patients with metabolic heart disease than in healthy hearts.
statements.evidence: hold significant clinical implications for treating metabolic syndrome-associated heart diseases.
statements.note: The abstract claims clinical relevance, but LIPTER levels in patient heart tissue were not measured.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LIPTER transgenic expression eased cardiac lipotoxicity, protected cardiac function, and alleviated cardiomyopathy in high-fat-diet-fed and Lepr db/db mice.
statements.evidence: LIPTER transgenic expression mitigates cardiac lipotoxicity, preserves cardiac function and alleviates cardiomyopathies in high-fat-diet-fed and Lepr db/db mice.
statements.note: Transgenic LIPTER reduced cardiac lipotoxicity, preserved function and alleviated cardiomyopathy in two mouse disease models.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deleting Myh10 in mouse cardiomyocytes caused lipid-droplet accumulation, reduced fatty acid oxidation, and compromised cardiac function.
statements.evidence: Conditional Myh10 deletion in mouse cardiomyocytes leads to LD accumulation, reduced fatty acid oxidation and compromised cardiac function.
statements.note: Conditional Myh10 deletion led to lipid-droplet accumulation, lower fatty acid oxidation and impaired cardiac function.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: LIPTER attaches to phosphatidic acid and PI4P on lipid-droplet membranes and to MYH10, linking droplets to the MYH10-ACTIN cytoskeleton to move them.
statements.evidence: LIPTER binds phosphatidic acid and phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate on LD surface membranes and the MYH10 protein, connecting LDs to the MYH10-ACTIN cytoskeleton and facilitating LD transport.
statements.note: LIPTER binds lipid-droplet-membrane phospholipids and MYH10, tethering droplets to the MYH10-ACTIN cytoskeleton for transport.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: mcPGK1 steers metabolic reprogramming by blocking mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and boosting glycolysis.
statements.evidence: mcPGK1 regulates metabolic reprogramming by inhibiting mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS) and promoting glycolysis.
statements.note: mcPGK1 reprograms metabolism by inhibiting mitochondrial OXPHOS and promoting glycolysis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: mcPGK1 promotes PGK1 import into mitochondria through TOM40 interactions, shifting metabolism from oxidative phosphorylation toward glycolysis.
statements.evidence: mcPGK1 promotes PGK1 mitochondrial import via TOM40 interactions, reprogramming metabolism from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis through PGK1-PDK1-PDH axis.
statements.note: mcPGK1 drives PGK1 import into mitochondria via TOM40, redirecting metabolism toward glycolysis through the PGK1-PDK1-PDH axis.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Silencing mcPGK1 sensitized liver tumour cells to chemotherapy.
statements.evidence: Liver tumour-initiating cells (TICs) contribute to tumour initiation, metastasis, progression and drug resistance.
statements.note: Drug resistance is attributed to TICs generally, but mcPGK1's effect on chemotherapy response was not tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down mcPGK1 impairs liver tumour-initiating-cell self-renewal, whereas overexpressing it drives their self-renewal.
statements.evidence: mcPGK1 knockdown impairs liver TIC self-renewal, whereas its overexpression drives liver TIC self-renewal.
statements.note: The study shows mcPGK1 knockdown impairs liver TIC self-renewal while its overexpression drives it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: lncHOME identifies coPARSE-lncRNAs, a class of lncRNAs whose genomic locations and RBP-binding-site patterns are conserved.
statements.evidence: a computational pipeline that identifies a unique class of long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) with conserved genomic locations and patterns of RNA-binding protein (RBP) binding sites (coPARSE-lncRNAs).
statements.note: lncHOME defines coPARSE-lncRNAs by their conserved genomic locations and conserved RBP-binding-site patterns.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: coPARSE-lncRNAs are absent from invertebrates such as Drosophila.
statements.evidence: several hundred human coPARSE-lncRNAs can be evolutionarily traced to zebrafish.
statements.note: Conservation is shown among vertebrates, but the abstract makes no claim about invertebrate species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking down coPARSE-lncRNAs in zebrafish embryos caused severe developmental delay, which human homologs rescued.
statements.evidence: Knocking down coPARSE-lncRNAs in zebrafish embryos caused severe developmental delays that were rescued by human homologs.
statements.note: Zebrafish embryos lacking coPARSE-lncRNAs showed severe developmental delay that human homologs reversed.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Knocking out many human coPARSE-lncRNAs produced cell-proliferation defects that predicted zebrafish homologs could rescue.
statements.evidence: we found that knocking out many human coPARSE-lncRNAs led to cell proliferation defects, which were subsequently rescued by predicted zebrafish homologs.
statements.note: Human coPARSE-lncRNA knockouts caused proliferation defects that predicted zebrafish homologs rescued.
